records.source: :mod:`spacr.ports` now declares what each module consumes and produces, and :mod:`spacr.artifacts` records where every finished run put its outputs.  This module joins the two:
records.translation: :mod:`spacr.ports` declara ahora lo que cada módulo consume y produce, y :mod:`spacr.artifacts` registra dónde dejó sus salidas cada ejecución terminada.  Este módulo une ambos:

records.context: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a setting name should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.label: spacr.chaining#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`chained_inputs` asks the registry — ``latest(kind, project=…)`` — where the upstream module's output *is*, and turns that into the value a settings key should hold.  The answer comes from the row the producer wrote, not from re-deriving ``<root>/merged``;
records.translation: :func:`chained_inputs` pregunta al registro —``latest(kind, project=…)``— dónde *está* la salida del módulo anterior y la convierte en el valor que debe contener una clave de configuración.  La respuesta procede de la fila que escribió el productor, no de volver a derivar ``<root>/merged``;

records.context: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings key-value mapping **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.label: spacr.chaining#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: :func:`resolve_settings` applies those values to a settings dict **without ever overwriting a path the user edited**.  A user edit is remembered in a :class:`PinStore` and takes precedence until it is cleared; when the upstream later moves, the new location is *offered* (:class:`HeldPin`) rather than pushed;
records.translation: :func:`resolve_settings` aplica esos valores a un diccionario de configuración **sin sobrescribir nunca una ruta que el usuario haya editado**.  Una edición del usuario se recuerda en un :class:`PinStore` y tiene prioridad hasta que se borra; cuando el módulo anterior cambia de ubicación más adelante, la nueva ubicación se *ofrece* (:class:`HeldPin`) en lugar de imponerse;

records.source: :func:`next_steps` lists the modules that can run on a finished run's outputs, using :func:`spacr.ports.next_modules` for the candidates, :func:`chained_inputs` for their pre-filled settings and :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` so a successor that *cannot* run is offered with its blocking reason.
records.translation: :func:`next_steps` enumera los módulos que pueden ejecutarse sobre las salidas de una ejecución terminada, usando :func:`spacr.ports.next_modules` para los candidatos, :func:`chained_inputs` para su configuración prellenada y :func:`spacr.ports.check_ready` para que un sucesor que *no puede* ejecutarse se ofrezca junto con el motivo que lo bloquea.

records.source: For every port ``module`` consumes, the registry is asked for the newest artifact of that kind in each candidate project, in order, and the first hit wins.  The answer is the row the *producer* wrote — its path, its project, its settings hash — so a plate whose merged arrays ended up somewhere unusual chains correctly, which re-deriving ``<root>/merged`` would not.
records.translation: Para cada puerto que consume ``module``, se pide al registro el artefacto más reciente de ese tipo en cada proyecto candidato, en orden, y gana la primera coincidencia. records.source: Resolve a dropped path against ``module``'s inputs.
records.translation: Resuelve una ruta soltada frente a las entradas de ``module``.

records.context: The resolution is the same one auto-chaining performs. For every input the module declares, the registry is asked first — :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.latest` for that kind in that project, as :func:`chained_inputs` asks it — so a drop and an auto-chain fill the field with the same string. Only when no run was ever registered does the declared layout in :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` answer instead, and then it answers with the folder the ports say it is in.
records.label: spacr.chaining.resolve_drop#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The resolution is the same one auto-chaining performs. For every input the module declares, the registry is asked first — :meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.latest` for that kind in that project, as :func:`chained_inputs` asks it — so a drop and an auto-chain fill the field with the same string. Only when no run was ever registered does the declared layout in :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS` answer instead, and then it answers with the folder the ports say it is in.
records.translation: La resolución es la misma que realiza el encadenamiento automático. Para cada entrada que declara el módulo, se consulta primero el registro (:meth:`spacr.artifacts.Registry.latest` para ese tipo en ese proyecto, tal como lo consulta :func:`chained_inputs`), de modo que una ruta soltada y un encadenamiento automático rellenan el campo con la misma cadena. Solo cuando nunca se registró ninguna ejecución responde en su lugar la estructura declarada en :data:`spacr.ports.PORTS`, y entonces responde con la carpeta en la que los puertos indican que se encuentra.

Keeping the state machine here gives the CV and ML implementations one clock and one ordering rule without importing FlowView on their disabled path. Its callables remain private; the module documentation explains why this instrumentation exists without promoting those helpers into the public API.
records.translation: Los módulos centrales de la canalización acceden a este módulo privado solo a través de una comprobación diferida de ``sys.modules``. Mantener aquí la máquina de estados proporciona a las implementaciones de CV y ML un único reloj y una única regla de ordenación sin importar FlowView en su ruta desactivada. Sus invocables siguen siendo privados; la documentación del módulo explica por qué existe esta instrumentación sin promover esos auxiliares a la API pública.

records.context: **Every download is atomic, and never overwrites.** Bytes stream into a temporary file *in the destination directory* (so the final ``os.replace`` is a same-filesystem rename, which is atomic) and the rename happens only after the checksum passes. An interrupted or cancelled download therefore leaves nothing behind that looks like a model — the failure mode where half a checkpoint sits at the real filename, loads, and segments badly, cannot happen.

records.translation: **Cada descarga es atómica y nunca sobrescribe.** Los bytes se transmiten a un archivo temporal *en el directorio de destino* (de modo que el ``os.replace`` final es un cambio de nombre dentro del mismo sistema de archivos, que es atómico) y el cambio de nombre solo se produce después de que la suma de comprobación sea correcta. Por tanto, una descarga interrumpida o cancelada no deja nada que parezca un modelo: no puede darse el caso de fallo en que medio punto de control queda con el nombre de archivo real, se carga y segmenta mal.

records.context: **Benchmarks are only comparable inside one field set.** A model's score on your three fields does not predict its score on somebody else's, and a table that sorts the two together produces a ranking of two unrelated numbers. So every :class:`BenchmarkResult` records a :func:`fieldset_id` — a hash of the actual pixels, not the folder name — and :func:`rank` **raises** :class:`IncomparableBenchmarks` when handed results from more than one field set. :func:`rank_groups` and :func:`format_benchmarks` are the supported alternative: they group by field set, rank within each group, and label the groups.

records.context: There is no ground truth here. :func:`benchmark` runs one model over N microscope fields of view and reports what came out: object counts, timings and the :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` verdict per microscope field of view (fused? shattered? empty? all on the border?). That is a *quality-control* score, not an accuracy — it can tell you a model collapsed on your data, it cannot tell you which of two plausible segmentations is right. :data:`RANK_KEYS` therefore offers exactly two structured-data names, ``'qc'`` and ``'seconds'``, and no structured-data name that would read as accuracy. To compare two models against each other, use :func:`compare_entries`, which hands both to :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — the A/B harness that is explicit about neither side being the truth.

records.source: There is no ground truth here. :func:`benchmark` runs one model over N fields and reports what came out: object counts, timings and the :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` verdict per field (fused? shattered? empty? all on the border?). That is a *quality-control* score, not an accuracy — it can tell you a model collapsed on your data, it cannot tell you which of two plausible segmentations is right. :data:`RANK_KEYS` therefore offers exactly two keys, ``'qc'`` and ``'seconds'``, and no key that would read as accuracy. To compare two models against each other, use :func:`compare_entries`, which hands both to :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models` — the A/B harness that is explicit about neither side being the truth.
records.translation: Aquí no hay datos de referencia. :func:`benchmark` ejecuta un modelo sobre N campos de imagen e informa de lo que se obtuvo: recuentos de objetos, tiempos y el veredicto de :mod:`spacr.seg_qc` por campo (¿fusionados?, ¿fragmentados?, ¿vacío?, ¿todo en el borde?). Es una puntuación de *control de calidad*, no una exactitud: puede indicar que un modelo fracasó con sus datos, pero no cuál de dos segmentaciones plausibles es la correcta. Por ello, :data:`RANK_KEYS` ofrece exactamente dos claves, ``'qc'`` y ``'seconds'``, y ninguna clave que pueda interpretarse como exactitud. Para comparar dos modelos entre sí, use :func:`compare_entries`, que pasa ambos a :func:`spacr.model_compare.compare_models`, el banco de pruebas A/B que deja explícito que ninguno de los dos lados es la verdad.

records.source: Safeguards
records.translation: Salvaguardas

records.context: **Every download is checksummed, and verification happens before use.** A checkpoint truncated by a dropped connection, or swapped for a different one at the same URL, still loads. It does not throw; it produces silently different masks, and the run that used it looks exactly like the run that did not. So :func:`fetch` hashes what arrived and compares it to the hash the catalogue published: a mismatch deletes the file and throws :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — the entry is never registered. The hash that was actually computed is stored on the returned entry, so "verified" means "these bytes", not "this filename".
records.label: spacr.model_zoo#9
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Every download is checksummed, and verification happens before use.** A checkpoint truncated by a dropped connection, or swapped for a different one at the same URL, still loads. It does not raise; it produces silently different masks, and the run that used it looks exactly like the run that did not. So :func:`fetch` hashes what arrived and compares it to the hash the catalogue published: a mismatch deletes the file and raises :class:`ChecksumMismatch` — the entry is never registered. The hash that was actually computed is stored on the returned entry, so "verified" means "these bytes", not "this filename".
records.translation: **Cada descarga se verifica con una suma de comprobación, y la verificación se realiza antes del uso.** Un punto de control truncado por una conexión interrumpida, o sustituido por otro distinto en la misma URL, sigue cargándose. No genera ninguna excepción; produce silenciosamente máscaras distintas, y la ejecución que lo usó parece exactamente igual que la que no lo usó. Por ello, :func:`fetch` calcula el hash de lo recibido y lo compara con el hash que publicó el catálogo: una discrepancia elimina el archivo y genera :class:`ChecksumMismatch`, y la entrada nunca se registra. El hash calculado realmente se almacena en la entrada devuelta, de modo que "verified" significa "these bytes", no "this filename".

records.context: ``'none'`` no hash at all — nothing can be checked, and :func:`fetch` refuses such an entry unless the caller overrides it. ``'published'`` a hash came with the entry but the bytes are not here yet; it is the digest the download will be checked against. ``'recorded'`` the hash of the file on disk is known, but no published digest exists to compare it against. records.source: ``'none'`` no hash at all — nothing can be checked, and :func:`fetch` refuses such an entry unless the caller overrides it. ``'published'`` a hash came with the entry but the bytes are not here yet; it is the digest the download will be checked against. ``'recorded'`` the hash of the file on disk is known, but no published digest exists to compare it against. It shows only that the file has not changed since the hash was recorded. ``'verified'`` the bytes on disk were compared with a published digest and match.
records.translation: ``'none'`` no hay ningún hash: no puede comprobarse nada, y :func:`fetch` rechaza una entrada así salvo que quien llama lo anule. ``'published'`` la entrada venía con un hash, pero los bytes aún no están aquí; es el resumen con el que se comprobará la descarga. ``'recorded'`` se conoce el hash del archivo en disco, pero no existe ningún resumen publicado con el que compararlo. Solo demuestra que el archivo no ha cambiado desde que se registró el hash. ``'verified'`` los bytes en disco se compararon con un resumen publicado y coinciden.

records.context: The rules, in order:
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The rules, in order:
records.translation: Las reglas, en orden:

records.context: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a machine-learning classification model checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.label: spacr.model_zoo.classify_kind#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: 1. ``*.CP_model`` is a Cellpose checkpoint — that is what :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` names its output. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` is a classifier checkpoint (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` writes ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **unless** it sits in a Cellpose folder or has ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` in its name. 3. An **extensionless** file inside a Cellpose folder is a Cellpose checkpoint only if its first bytes are a torch save. ``cellpose.train`` writes ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` with no suffix, and that folder also holds READMEs and logs — the magic-byte check is what keeps a ``README`` out of the zoo. 4. Anything else is not a model. CSVs, PNGs, ``.npy`` masks and settings snapshots all land here and are ignored.
records.translation: 1. ``*.CP_model`` es un punto de control de Cellpose: así nombra :func:`spacr.submodules.train_cellpose` su salida. 2. ``*.pth`` / ``*.pt`` es un punto de control de clasificador (:func:`spacr.io._save_model` escribe ``<model_type>_epoch_<n>_channels_<ch>.pth``) **salvo que** se encuentre en una carpeta de Cellpose o tenga ``cellpose``/``cp_model`` en su nombre. 3. Un archivo **sin extensión** dentro de una carpeta de Cellpose es un punto de control de Cellpose solo si sus primeros bytes corresponden a un guardado de torch. ``cellpose.train`` escribe ``<save_path>/models/<name>`` sin sufijo, y esa carpeta también contiene READMEs y registros; la comprobación de bytes mágicos es lo que mantiene un ``README`` fuera del catálogo. 4. Todo lo demás no es un modelo. Los CSVs, los PNGs, las máscaras ``.npy`` y las instantáneas de configuración van a parar aquí y se ignoran.

records.context: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.

records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: The post-processing of empanada's Panoptic-DeepLab models, ported so spaCR does not depend on empanada-dl. A pixel is mitochondrion when ``semantic`` reaches ``threshold``. Instance centres are the local maxima of ``centres`` in a ``centre_window`` square that reach ``centre_threshold``. Each mitochondrion pixel votes, through its ``offsets`` (row, column), for the place its centre is, and joins the nearest centre found. Instances smaller than ``min_size`` pixels are dropped and the rest are numbered 1..n in raster order of their centres.
records.translation: El posprocesamiento de los modelos Panoptic-DeepLab de empanada, portado para que spaCR no dependa de empanada-dl. Un píxel es mitocondria cuando ``semantic`` alcanza ``threshold``. Los centros de las instancias son los máximos locales de ``centres`` en un cuadrado ``centre_window`` que alcanzan ``centre_threshold``. Cada píxel de mitocondria vota, mediante sus ``offsets`` (fila, columna), por el lugar en que se encuentra su centro, y se une al centro más cercano encontrado. Las instancias menores de ``min_size`` píxeles se descartan y las restantes se numeran 1..n en orden de barrido de sus centros.

records.context: ``spacr.ml.regression_model`` can return a statsmodels ``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, ``QuantReg``, a ``GLM`` in any of six families, a ``MixedLM``, a ``BetaModel``, a sklearn ``Lasso``/``Ridge``/``ElasticNet`` or a ``LinearSVC``. Those objects agree on almost nothing: a sklearn ``Lasso`` has no p-values, no covariance matrix and no ``fittedvalues``; a ``MixedLM`` has no hat matrix; a Gaussian model has no calibration curve worth drawing. Every panel therefore either draws or raises :class:`PanelUnavailable` carrying the *reason*, and the reason is printed on the combined report page and returned in the manifest. A panel is never silently omitted, and never faked with a substitute statistic that does not mean what the axis label says.

Those objects agree on almost nothing: a sklearn ``Lasso`` has no p-values, no covariance matrix and no ``fittedvalues``; a ``MixedLM`` has no hat matrix; a Gaussian model has no calibration curve worth drawing. Every panel therefore either draws or raises :class:`PanelUnavailable` carrying the *reason*, and the reason is printed on the combined report page and returned in the manifest. A panel is never silently omitted, and never faked with a substitute statistic that does not mean what the axis label says.
records.translation: ``spacr.ml.regression_model`` puede devolver un ``OLS``, ``WLS``, ``RLM``, ``QuantReg`` de statsmodels, un ``GLM`` de cualquiera de seis familias, un ``MixedLM``, un ``BetaModel``, un ``Lasso``/``Ridge``/``ElasticNet`` de sklearn o un ``LinearSVC``. Esos objetos no coinciden en casi nada: un ``Lasso`` de sklearn no tiene p-values, ni matriz de covarianza, ni ``fittedvalues``; un ``MixedLM`` no tiene matriz sombrero; un modelo gaussiano no tiene ninguna curva de calibración que merezca la pena dibujar. Por ello, cada panel o bien se dibuja o bien genera :class:`PanelUnavailable` con el *motivo*, y el motivo se imprime en la página combinada del informe y se devuelve en el manifiesto. Un panel nunca se omite en silencio, ni se falsea con un estadístico sustituto que no significa lo que dice la etiqueta del eje.

records.context: Treating all of those as "the error variance of ``y - fitted``" is how a QC panel reports the wrong microplate sample positions as outliers, in a direction that depends on the units of the response. records.source: Treating all of those as "the error variance of ``y - fitted``" is how a QC panel reports the wrong wells as outliers, in a direction that depends on the units of the response. A hinge/SVM has no likelihood at all, so it is not binomial — but it is the one model spaCR offers whose whole output is a discrimination, which is what ROC and precision-recall measure. records.source: Separate from :attr:`is_binomial`, which asks whether a *binomial likelihood* was fitted. Excluding it from those two panels, which is what asking only :attr:`is_binomial` did, left the classifier as the single model type with no discrimination QC.
records.translation: Es independiente de :attr:`is_binomial`, que pregunta si se ajustó una *verosimilitud binomial*. records.source: Return the condition number of a design matrix, scaled and unscaled.
records.translation: Devuelve el número de condición de una matriz de diseño, escalado y sin escalar.

records.context: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.
records.label: spacr.regression_qc.condition_number#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Two numbers, because they answer different questions. The *unscaled* condition number is what ``statsmodels`` prints in a summary, and it is dominated by the units of the columns: a predictor measured in cells rather than thousands of cells changes it by 1000 with no change in the science. The *scaled* one (each column normalised to unit length first, the Belsley-Kuh-Welsch definition) is unit-free and is the one whose thresholds — 30, 100, 1000 — mean anything.
records.translation: Dos números, porque responden a preguntas distintas. El número de condición *sin escalar* es el que imprime ``statsmodels`` en un resumen, y está dominado por las unidades de las columnas: un predictor medido en células en lugar de miles de células lo cambia en un factor de 1000 sin que cambie nada en la ciencia. El *escalado* (cada columna normalizada antes a longitud unitaria, la definición de Belsley-Kuh-Welsch) no tiene unidades y es aquel cuyos umbrales (30, 100, 1000) significan algo.

records.context: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Under a correctly specified Poisson model ``phi == 1``. ``phi`` well above 1 means the standard errors are too small by ``sqrt(phi)`` — at ``phi = 6``, a 2.4-fold inflation, which turns noise into a screening experiment full of hits. That is why this number is on the report as a number and not as a shape to eyeball.
records.label: spacr.regression_qc.overdispersion_statistic#1
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Under a correctly specified Poisson model ``phi == 1``. ``phi`` well above 1 means the standard errors are too small by ``sqrt(phi)`` — at ``phi = 6``, a 2.4-fold inflation, which turns noise into a screen full of hits. That is why this number is on the report as a number and not as a shape to eyeball.
records.translation: ``phi = sum((y - mu)^2 / V(mu)) / df_resid``. Con un modelo de Poisson correctamente especificado, ``phi == 1``. Un ``phi`` muy superior a 1 significa que los errores estándar son demasiado pequeños en un factor de ``sqrt(phi)``: con ``phi = 6``, una inflación de 2.4 veces, que convierte el ruido en un cribado lleno de aciertos. Por eso este número figura en el informe como número y no como una forma que se valora a ojo.

records.source: Computed from the inverse of the predictor *correlation* matrix — the identity ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj`` — rather than by running ``p`` auxiliary regressions. On a screen design with 1,200 gRNA columns the auxiliary- regression route is ``O(p^4)`` and is impractical; the correlation route is one ``O(p^3)`` decomposition. records.translation: Se calcula a partir de la inversa de la matriz de *correlación* de los predictores (la identidad ``VIF_j = (R^-1)_jj``) en lugar de ejecutar ``p`` regresiones auxiliares. records.context: **A column with no values at all comes back as** ``object``. This is the common one and it is not a data problem: ``pandas.read_sql`` builds the frame from the rows it gets, so a column that is ``NULL`` in every row arrives as a column of ``None`` and pandas types that ``object`` -- even though SQLite declares it ``REAL``. spaCR writes ``NULL`` for a NaN, and whole measurements are legitimately NaN for a whole database: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` are NaN for every uniform object, and ``mode_intensity`` was NaN for every object in every database written before the SciPy shim in ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Such a column is converted to ``float64`` NaN, which is what it always meant. Nothing is lost, so nothing is warned about -- and the caller's own all-NaN filter then drops it and says so.

records.translation: **Una columna sin ningún valor se devuelve como** ``object``. Es el caso habitual y no es un problema de datos: ``pandas.read_sql`` construye la tabla a partir de las filas que recibe, de modo que una columna que es ``NULL`` en todas las filas llega como una columna de ``None`` y pandas le asigna el tipo ``object``, aunque SQLite la declare ``REAL``. spaCR escribe ``NULL`` para un NaN, y hay mediciones completas que son legítimamente NaN en toda una base de datos: ``skew_intensity``/``kurtosis_intensity`` son NaN para todo objeto uniforme, y ``mode_intensity`` era NaN para todos los objetos de todas las bases de datos escritas antes del parche de SciPy en ``measure._extended_regionprops_table``. Una columna así se convierte a NaN de tipo ``float64``, que es lo que siempre significó. No se pierde nada, por lo que no se advierte de nada -- y el propio filtro de quien llama para columnas totalmente NaN la descarta después y lo indica.
